clue.text: Second thoughts about part of navy's weaponry

indicators.note: about means going round, so the ideas surround the naval piece

parts.note: thoughts are ideas
the Royal Marines, RM, are part of the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A sailor reconsiders some of the navy's armaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts RM inside IDEAS after S. The Royal Marines are the navy's soldiers, a British convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidearms are pistols and other small weapons carried at the belt, a kind of weaponry.

clue.text: Educationalist wears smart clothing to work for press

indicators.note: wears means the teacher is clothed in, so placed within, the outfit

parts.note: a suit is smart clothing
BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree, so an educationalist

explanation.surface: A teacher dons a suit to take a job with a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: BEd (Bachelor of Education) is the British teaching degree; 'wears' means the graduate is inside the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to prepare copy for printing, a newspaper task.

clue.text: Absolute rule has place in religious belief

indicators.note: in signals that the location word sits inside the faith word

parts.note: deism is belief in a creator god without revelation
a spot is a place

explanation.surface: Total authority finds room within a creed.
explanation.walkthrough: Deism is belief in a creator who does not intervene; 'has' is a link and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Despotism is government by a single ruler with unlimited power.

clue.text: Severe wind from South and East

parts.note: Auster is the Latin name for the south wind

explanation.surface: A harsh wind blowing from the south and east.
explanation.walkthrough: AUSTER is the classical south wind, a crossword stock word.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere means stern and strict, as severe does.

clue.text: Cuts down the totality of invading plants

indicators.note: invading means the totality word enters the cutting word

parts.note: mows means cuts down grass or crops
all is the totality

explanation.surface: Someone scythes through every invasive weed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuts down' reads as the definition's verb but is the outer piece; 'invading' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallows are flowering plants of the family that includes the hollyhock.

clue.text: Amount of money Us university required for the highest degree

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money
MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is an American university

explanation.surface: A large fee charged by an American college for its top qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degree' suggests an academic award, but here it means extent: the highest degree of anything is its peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A summit is the topmost point, so figuratively the utmost extent or level.

clue.text: Procrustes, so to speak, making one lie here

definitions.meaning: the Greek villain racked guests to fit his bed, so he was one who elongated people
a portable bed for carrying an injured person, on which one is laid

explanation.surface: The legendary torturer forces his victim onto a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Procrustes stretched victims who were too short for his bed. A stretcher is also an exaggeration, a lie, which colours the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is both one who stretches and a frame for carrying the sick lying down.

clue.text: Endless din upset fellow going over house

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means placed on top of the following piece

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the shortened noise word is read upwards
endless means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: din is noise

explanation.surface: A man, disturbed by unending racket, crosses to a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' trims NOISE to NOIS and 'upset' turns it to SION, with MAN 'going over' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mansion is a large, grand house.

clue.text: Prohibited drug taken by sick girl

indicators.note: taken by means held within, so the drug sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ill means sick
gal is an informal word for a girl
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An ill young woman takes a banned substance.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a common crossword convention; 'taken by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Illegal means forbidden by law.

clue.text: Finest source of wines, say, for popular author

parts.note: finest means best

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a store of wine is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds identical

parts.note: wines are fetched from a cellar

explanation.surface: Praising the best wine merchant as a literary favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns CELLAR into SELLER, which sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: An author whose books sell in great numbers is called a bestseller.

clue.text: A swan lacking space can be seen on this river

definitions.text: A swan lacking space can be seen on this river

parts.words: A swan lacking space can be seen on this river
parts.note: close up the gap in the words 'A swan' and you get Aswan, the Egyptian city and dam beside the river in question

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher notes that a cramped swan is visible on a particular river.
explanation.walkthrough: The swan is a red herring: delete the space between 'A' and 'swan' to get ASWAN, the city and High Dam on this river.
explanation.definitionFit: Aswan stands on Egypt's great river, famous for the High Dam built across it.

clue.text: Act in character? It's Lorna's personal obsession

parts.note: Lorna Doone is the heroine of R. D. Blackmore's novel, so her surname with the possessive gives these letters
personal means one's own
a thing, as in 'he has a thing about trains', is an obsession

explanation.surface: Asking whether the heroine's private fixation explains her behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: LORNA DOONE is a 19th-century English romance set on Exmoor; only her surname is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To behave in one's own characteristic way, independently of others, is the idiom meant.

clue.text: Muscle shown by church probing effects of drug abuse

indicators.note: probing means going into, so the church abbreviation sits inside the drug experiences

parts.note: trips are hallucinatory experiences from drugs such as LSD
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A muscle displayed while a church investigates the results of narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' is the container signal; 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The triceps is the large muscle at the back of the upper arm.

clue.text: They live on another location captured by airborne troops

indicators.note: captured by means held inside, so the location is enclosed by the troops

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Settlers on another site are seized by parachutists.
explanation.walkthrough: PARAS is the British short form for the Parachute Regiment; 'captured by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Parasites are organisms that feed off a host creature.

clue.text: Pebbles one only found around end of beach

indicators.note: around means the word for one alone encircles the final letter

parts.note: a single thing is one only

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A lone pebble discovered at the far end of the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts H, the last letter of 'beach', inside SINGLE; 'found' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingle is a mass of small rounded stones on a beach.

clue.text: Binding agreement to rebuild gate near university

indicators.note: to rebuild means to construct again, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A contract to reconstruct the gate beside the campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuild' rearranges GATE NEAR with U.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal assurance or pledge, a binding promise.

clue.text: Meat and food taken back in German city

parts.note: ham is a meat

indicators.note: taken back means the word for food is read in reverse

parts.note: grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Someone returns a meal of ham while in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns GRUB into BURG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamburg is a major port city in northern Germany.

clue.text: Pistol, for example, is antique

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare's swaggering soldier is called ... Pistol, ... being an old word for ensign

explanation.surface: An old firearm counts as an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is not a gun: he is the braggart in Henry IV and Henry V, holding the rank of ancient (ensign).
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient means very old, and was also the rank of standard-bearer.

clue.text: Told to wrap three-quarters of a stone in rich fabric

indicators.note: to wrap means to enclose, so the past-tense command word goes round the shortened stone

parts.note: bade is a past tense of bid, meaning told or ordered

indicators.note: three-quarters of a four-letter word means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: Instructed to wrap most of a gem in luxurious cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-quarters of' keeps three of the four letters, and 'to wrap' is the container signal; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven fabric with a raised pattern.

clue.text: Expedition finds oil, naturally, going round South America

indicators.note: going round means the oil word surrounds the continent abbreviation

parts.note: crude is oil in its natural, unrefined state

explanation.surface: Prospectors strike oil on a journey around South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil, naturally' is crude oil, untreated; 'going round' is the container signal and 'finds' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade was a military expedition, and the word now means any vigorous campaign.

clue.text: Toast revolutionary English leader with port

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Drinking the health of a revolutionary English chief with port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the wine, but it is Rio; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is an informal farewell, also used as a drinking salutation like cheers.

clue.text: Like Keats's sweeter melodies — nearly a hundred arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put in order afresh, so the letters are reordered as in a musical arrangement
nearly means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A poet's sweetest tunes, nearly a hundred of them set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts A HUNDRED to AHUNDRE and 'arranged' rearranges it. Keats's Ode on a Grecian Urn says 'Heard melodies are sweet, but those unheard are sweeter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Keats's line says melodies never actually listened to are sweeter still.

clue.text: Came on stage and made a record

definitions.meaning: an actor making an entrance comes on stage
to make a record of something is to write it down in a log

explanation.surface: A performer walked on and cut a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' suggests a music recording, but it means logging something in writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Entered means both walked in and wrote down in a register.

clue.text: Make a pledge before having death-wish?

definitions.text: Make a pledge before having death-wish?

parts.words: Make a pledge before having death-wish?
parts.note: the oath formula for swearing truthfulness continues 'and hope to die', so the vow comes just before a wish to die

explanation.surface: Someone takes a vow and then wishes to be dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The children's oath runs 'cross my heart and hope to die', so the pledge is followed by a 'death-wish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the sign over one's chest is a gesture of swearing that what one says is true.

clue.text: She takes very long time

parts.note: an era is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A woman spends ages over something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's name, so a female person can be referred to as she.

clue.text: Threat reef represented from then on

indicators.note: represented read as re-presented means set out afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A danger posed by coral has been portrayed ever since.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges THREAT REEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereafter is an adverb meaning after that time, subsequently.

clue.text: Female teacher abandons motorway? It's the pressure

indicators.note: abandons means the road letters are left out of the teacher word

parts.note: a schoolmistress, or mistress, is a female teacher
the M1 is Britain's main motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: A schoolmistress quits the motorway because the strain is too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's London-to-Yorkshire motorway; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is pressure or tension, physical or mental.

clue.text: Aquatic plant propagated deep down

indicators.note: propagated means bred or spread, suggesting the letters are reproduced in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A water plant grown far below the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'propagated' rearranges DEEP DOWN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pondweed is a general name for plants growing submerged in still water.
